{{nihongo|'''Sanai Shrine'''|左内神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izu Province]].

{{wikidata link|Q134926924|ja|左内神社|grok=none|check_date=2026-07-06}}

=== Overview ===
It is situated in the southwestern part of Mishima City’s Nakajima district, between the {{ill|Gotengawa River|ja|御殿川|qid=Q18988494}} and the Nakajima Community Center.

It is identified with the {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} '''Fuminashi Shrine''' (ふみなしじんじゃ) / '''Chichinashi Shrine''' (ちちなしじんじゃ), or '''Ametsuseketachi-no-Mikoto Shrine''' (あめつせけたちのみことじんじゃ).<ref name="city1">[https://www.city.mishima.shizuoka.jp/ipn030092.html Sanai Shrine] - Mishima City</ref><ref name="city2">[https://www.city.mishima.shizuoka.jp/mishima_info/amenity/rekishi/jinja/jinnja.htm Shrines] - Mishima City</ref>

The date of its founding is unknown, but it is said that, as its name suggests, it once stood on the east side (the left side when viewed from Mishima Taisha) of the old Shimoda Highway, which also served as the approach to {{ill|Mishima Taisha|Q650772|qid=Q650772}}.<ref name="city1"/>

More specifically, it is said to have originally stood to the north of its present location, near the Tenashi (てなし) Jizō in the Naka district. According to one theory, both Tenashi (てなし) and Chichinashi (ちちなし) (→ Fuminashi (ふみなし)) are corruptions of '''tetenashi''' (父梨/父無).<ref name="city1"/>

From there it was relocated south to the area around the present Nakajima Water Purification Plant (there is a stone monument to this effect), but in February of Meiji 19 (1886) it was damaged by a fire that destroyed all of its buildings, resulting in the loss of all treasures and ancient documents.<ref name="city1"/><ref name="city2"/> It was subsequently relocated and rebuilt at its current site in April of Meiji 20 (1887), and was renovated in Shōwa 16 (1941), remaining as it is today.<ref name="city2"/>

=== Enshrined deity ===
* Ametsuseketachi-no-Mikoto (阿米都瀬気多知命)
